builder_plan.scenario: Profiling shows attention computation is a bottleneck in your self-hosted service.
builder_plan.change: Check the supported GPU, tensor shapes, and precision, then replace only the relevant kernel.
builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Flow-based Spectral Kernel Learning for Nonstationary Attention
summary: FSKA replaces fixed or stationary kernelized attention (and standard query-key projection attention) with a learned nonstationary spectral kernel parameterized by normalizing flows, eliminating query--key projections and using fixed orthogonal value projections. Costs include the added complexity of normalizing-flow spectral density estimation, potential instability in learning spectral densities, and the implementation overhead of a custom linear-attention kernel. After adoption, the flow-based spectral density may fail to regularize properly on out-of-distribution sequence lengths or tasks, the orthogonal value projection constraint may degrade representational capacity for certain modalities, and the 40%--47% parameter reduction may not translate to end-to-end latency gains if flow computation becomes the bottleneck.
rationale: FSKA offers a concrete parameter-efficiency mechanism compatible with linear attention and a 24GB GPU budget, but the spectral density learning and flow components require empirical validation on the reader's specific classification or sequence tasks before production deployment.

claims.statement: FSKA replaces fixed or stationary kernelized attention (and standard query-key projection attention) with a learned nonstationary spectral kernel parameterized by normalizing flows, eliminating query--key projections and using fixed orthogonal value projections. Costs include the added complexity of normalizing-flow spectral density estimation, potential instability in learning spectral densities, and the implementation overhead of a custom linear-attention kernel. After adoption, the flow-based spectral density may fail to regularize properly on out-of-distribution sequence lengths or tasks, the orthogonal value projection constraint may degrade representational capacity for certain modalities, and the 40%--47% parameter reduction may not translate to end-to-end latency gains if flow computation becomes the bottleneck.

Reduces projection-related trainable parameters by approximately 40%--47% compared with most baselines while maintaining favorable linear-attention memory scaling; competitive or improved performance on classification, ablation, and scalability profiling.
